explanation: One line of argument holds that integration and later the euro removed the exchange-rate adjustment and cheapened credit, producing the debt accumulation and loss of competitiveness that ended in the 2011 request for assistance.

dispute.text: The counter-argument locates the crisis in domestic choices — the allocation of credit to non-tradable sectors, fiscal policy, and the failure to raise productivity — which membership permitted but did not dictate; on that reading the 1986 accession is context, not cause.
